newsitem.title: INDIA: Fiat plans to invest $1.0 billion in India.
newsitem.headline: Fiat plans to invest $1.0 billion in India.

text.p: Italy's Fiat SpA said on Monday it plans to invest a total of $1.0 billion in the five-year period from 1997 to 2002 in all the group's projects in India.
Fiat's chief executive officer Paolo Cantarella told a news conference that Fiat's Indian unit will start producing its Palio "world car" in 1999 in India in the western state of Maharashtra.
"The investment programmes we have launched or are now planning in this country will be worth $1.0 billion between 1997 and 2002," Cantarella said.

"We shall be making cars in Maharashtra state; by late 1999 this will be producing the first of its Palio cars and once fully operational it will be turning out around 100,000 of them every year," he added.

India in March approved a proposal for a $558 million joint venture between Fiat and India's Doshi family, which controls Premier Automobiles to produce cars. Fiat holds 74 percent of the joint venture.

The joint venture plans to build a new plant near the western city of Pune. Indian analysts project the domestic car market in the world's second most populous nation to grow to around one million units in 2000/2001 (April/March) from 345,355 in 1995/96.
